key_idea: Embed an unstable 2D vortex into 3D by placing it as a vortex ring at a very large distance from the axis of symmetry, where axisymmetric Euler locally converges to 2D Euler.
reason: The proof ingeniously bypasses the lack of explicit unstable 3D flows by lifting a known 2D instability into a 3D vortex ring of large radius. Using clean functional analytic arguments to pass from 2D Euler to 3D Navier-Stokes, this highly conceptual approach yields a historic result with a surprisingly transparent and inevitable structure.
recognized: Albritton, Brué, Colombo (2022) Non-uniqueness of Leray solutions of the 3D Navier-Stokes equations
